messages.content:
Assign the three-character ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category. Here are worked examples, then the case to code.

Example 1
Hospital course: A 72-year-old man with a 50 pack-year smoking history was admitted with three days of worsening breathlessness and purulent sputum. Spirometry showed an FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.52. He was treated with nebulised bronchodilators, oral prednisolone and antibiotics for an infective exacerbation of his long-standing airflow limitation.
Answer: J44

Example 2
Hospital course: A 58-year-old man presented with crushing central chest pain radiating to the jaw. The electrocardiogram showed ST elevation in the anterior leads and high-sensitivity troponin rose from 40 to 2100 ng/L. He underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention with a stent to the proximal left anterior descending artery.
Answer: I21

Example 3
Hospital course: A 34-year-old woman presented with fever, rigors, dysuria and right flank tenderness. Urine microscopy showed pyuria and culture grew Escherichia coli. Computed tomography showed a swollen right kidney with no abscess. She improved on intravenous ceftriaxone.
Answer: N10

Hospital course:
Hospital Course:

The patient was admitted with cough, weight loss, and a cavity in the right upper pulmonary lobe. The patient tested positive for HIV and was diagnosed with tuberculosis infection. After starting antiviral and anti-tuberculosis therapy, the patient presented with urinary retention due to an enlarged prostate. The patient was transferred to a tertiary care hospital for further management.

Assessment and Plan:

During the hospital stay, the patient underwent several diagnostic tests including sputum culture, smear, and interferon-γ release assay, which were negative for Mycobacterium tuberculosis. Lumbar puncture indicated nearly normal cerebrospinal fluid profile, and CT scan revealed a cavity with effusion in the upper right lung. Bronchoscopy confirmed the presence of Cryptococcus neoformans in the bronchoalveolar lavage fluid. Enhanced MRI of the prostate showed an abnormal patchy signal in the central gland of the prostate with reduced T2W1 signal in the seminal vesicles and peripheral zone of the prostate. A prostatic biopsy revealed granulomatous inflammation with positive periodic acid–Schiff staining. Culture of the prostatic tissue grew Cryptococcus neoformans.

The patient was diagnosed with AIDS with pulmonary cryptococcosis and cryptococcal prostatitis. Oral voriconazole and flucytosine combination therapy for 2 months followed by oral fluconazole maintenance treatment for 4 months was initiated and relieved the patient’s urinary retention and the cryptococcal prostatitis.
Discharge Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Discharge Plan:

The patient was discharged in stable condition with a prescription for oral fluconazole. The patient was advised to follow up with an infectious disease specialist for further management of the underlying condition of AIDS. The patient was also advised to take necessary precautions to prevent future infections.

Answer with the three-character category only.

text:
This case is HIV disease with cryptococcosis (pulmonary and prostatic). In ICD-10-AM, HIV disease resulting in other infectious and parasitic diseases is coded B20, and cryptococcosis is B45. Coding rules make B20 the principal diagnosis when HIV disease presents with an associated infection, and the specific infection (B45) is added as an additional code.

The tuberculosis was not confirmed. Sputum culture, smear and interferon-γ release assay were all negative, and cryptococcus was found instead. The final diagnosis is AIDS with cryptococcal infection.

B20 is the best fit for the principal diagnosis. It covers HIV disease resulting in infectious and parasitic diseases, with B20.5 as the subcode for HIV disease resulting in other mycoses.

**B20**
